question:
In the following question, the first and the last parts of the sentence/passage are numbered 1 and 6. The rest of the sentence/passage is split into four parts — P, Q, R, and S. These four parts are not given in their proper order. Read the sentence/passage and find the most logical order of the parts between 1 and 6.

The invention of the wheel changed the world.

P: Transport became easier.

Q: Machines could now be built.

R: Travel became faster.

S. Roads improved quickly.

6. It was a great invention.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph starts with the invention of the wheel, which dramatically changed the world.
 
• **Sentence P comes first** as it logically follows the invention of the wheel, stating how transport became easier:
 
 
• "Transport became easier."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R follows** as it elaborates on the impact of transport, mentioning faster travel:
 
 
• "Travel became faster."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S comes next** as it discusses the improvement of roads, which is a logical consequence of enhanced transport and travel:
 
 
• "Roads improved quickly."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q concludes** as it introduces the broader technological impact, mentioning the construction of machines:
 
 
• "Machines could now be built."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PRSQ**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"The invention of the wheel changed the world. Transport became easier. Travel became faster. Roads improved quickly. Machines could now be built. It was a great invention."
